subject: POC structure: duration vs credit-smoothing framework
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@orchidhealth.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot run cadence — handling bursty volumes and extension options

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We're approaching the last 2 weeks of our 6-week pilot and the engineering team has hit a couple of unexpected load patterns: short-term bursts during nightly batch validations that are causing us to eat through the remaining credits faster than we forecasted.

Two questions:
1) If we extend the pilot by 3 weeks to validate the integration at scale, what are the options you typically give customers for moving from a strict time-box to a credit-smoothing approach (so we don't run out during spike windows)?
2) Are there any one-off discounts or a temporary higher token bucket you can provide while we finish the data migration? Our procurement team will need something defined to approve another PO.

Appreciate a quick sketch of options. I can share our usage spreadsheet if it helps.

Best,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of ML Ops, Orchid Health
[Attachment: ORCH_Pilot_Usage_Q3.xlsx]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@orchidhealth.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot run cadence — handling bursty volumes and extension options

Hi Sam — great to hear the demo traction. Thanks for the usage file (got it attached).

Summary of practical options we see customers take:
- Short extension (2-4 weeks) + one-time credit top-up: we add a small block of tokens (prepaid credits) at a promotional rate to cover spikes; preserves time-box but reduces churn risk.
- Duration extension + credit smoothing: extend the pilot and move to a weekly averaged consumption allowance (we smooth bursts across the extension window). This requires a short SOW amendment to clarify measurement windows and rollover rules.
- Temporary elevated burst capacity: provide a limited elevated concurrency/burst SLA for the final 2 weeks to prevent throttling while you migrate. This is operational (no pricing change) but gated on usage caps.

For Orchid, given the batch-validation spikes, I recommend the "extension + credit smoothing" approach — it keeps the experiment open, gives you steady coverage for spikes, and is clean from billing perspective. I've attached a draft SOW amendment and a simple credit-smoothing illustration.

Next steps I propose:
1) I share the SOW-draft-v2.pdf and our estimated top-up (line item) for the credit bucket.
2) Kimberly and Priyom will confirm the promotional uplift we can offer (discount on top-up).
3) If acceptable, procurement issues a PO and we apply the amendment.

Kimberly / Priyom — quick read and flag any constraints (legal/finance) we should mention to Sam.

Cheers,
David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW-draft-v2.pdf, POC_Usage_Estimates.xlsx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot run cadence — handling bursty volumes and extension options

Thanks David — quick notes from finance/legal perspective: 
- We can offer a 15% promotional discount on a one-time credit top-up if the PO is issued within 5 business days. The top-up should be scoped as non-refundable, applied to the pilot account, and valid for 30 days.
- For the smoothing amendment (duration + weekly averaged allowance), we need the usage windows defined in writing (UTC week boundaries) and a clause that we reserve the right to re-evaluate if sustained consumption exceeds 300% of projected weekly average for two consecutive weeks.
- If Orchid prefers a temporary burst SLA (no pricing change), we can enable it but will require a temporary capacity reservation (internal change) and a visible note in the Console that it's a managed exception.

Hannah — can you confirm whether engineering has capacity to enable the temporary burst flag for the final 10 days if procurement can't move fast?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@orchidhealth.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot run cadence — handling bursty volumes and extension options

David / team — really helpful, thanks. Procurement asked for a clear option set they can approve quickly. Our preference is:
- 3-week extension (starts Sept 1)
- Credit-smoothing model: weekly averaged allowance with a one-time credit top-up of 200k tokens at 12% off list (your promo)
- If our weekly consumption exceeds 250% of the projected weekly average for two weeks in a row, revert to temporary burst capacity (you can trigger it) and we will revisit pricing.

I've attached the signed internal memo and procurement will issue the PO once they get the SOW amendment with the discount line items. Please send the editable SOW and an invoice/PO-ready quote.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of ML Ops, Orchid Health
[Attachment: ORCH_Internal_Memo.pdf]
